## Continuous closure and a strict solve {#continuous-closure}

The experimental integration addresses three distinct failure mechanisms:
a discontinuous transport closure near admissibility boundaries, an iteration
whose stabilization can change its nonlinear target, and unsuccessful proposals
being allowed to advance a state. The completed method combines closure
regularization with a strict native Newton solve and adaptive rollback
([the new research baseline uses a continuous guarded closure, Newton trials accepted only after residual decrease, and adaptive rollback of the complete state and auxiliary data]{.claim}[C-304](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-304){.cid .st-measured}). The final test does not isolate a single change as the
cause of success.

Let $c_s$ be an admissible surrogate coefficient and $c_f$ the existing fallback.
For a normalized margin $m$ into an accepted domain, define

$$
S(z)=\begin{cases}0&z\leq0,\\z^2(3-2z)&0<z<1,\\1&z\geq1.\end{cases}
\qquad c=c_f+w(c_s-c_f).
$$

The weight is a product of smooth margin factors for the model input box,
wrapper box, low heat coefficients and coefficient caps. It vanishes when the
declared guard test on the actual candidate rejects it. Invalid surrogate values
are masked to finite fallback *before* multiplication, so zero weight cannot
carry an inadmissible NaN into the result. The original model weights and
admissible domains stay fixed. This changes the closure near its boundaries;
continuity is not permission to extrapolate outside the guard.

Particle transport also needs a smooth handover between its diffusion and
convection representations. The candidate uses complementary weights around
the existing normalized density-gradient threshold. Both coefficient branches
remain finite before blending. Native radial coefficient smoothing stays fixed
in the ensemble test. A local conversion identity does not prove that later
coefficient smoothing and finite-volume interpolation preserve particle flux.
A direct particle-flux formulation has not been used for this pass.

The implicit time step uses the native unstabilized finite-volume residual.
Newton differentiates that residual and solves its linearized system. Its line
search accepts a finite trial only when the actual residual decreases by the
declared Armijo rule. Failure retains the previous accepted Newton iterate and
returns failure metadata. An optimizer's termination or a native status flag
alone does not establish physical acceptance.

## Physical acceptance and rejected-step rollback {#rejected-step-rollback}

For each evolving physical channel, retain cell terms $s$, $t$ and $q$ for
storage, transport and combined sources, with cell widths $\Delta\rho_j$.
The independent auditor reconstructs

$$
\eta_k=\frac{\sum_j|s_{jk}-(t_{jk}+q_{jk})|\,\Delta\rho_j}
{\sum_j(|s_{jk}|+|t_{jk}|+|q_{jk}|)\,\Delta\rho_j}.
$$

The terms are grouped before normalization exactly as in the declared physical
equation. Finite positive reference scales are required. Separate global balance
ratios include storage, edge flux, sources and pinning. The exact native residual
is retained independently of these physical channel ratios. Acceptance requires
all channel gates, global balance, finite profiles, positive temperatures and density, finite quantities of
interest and a successful solver flag. An explicit sawtooth reset stops this
validation. [maximum accepted physical-channel L1 is 1.76 × 10^−9^ against a 10^−8^ gate, and native mean L1 is 1.01 × 10^−14^ against 10^−10^; no crash occurs]{.claim}[C-307](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-307){.cid .st-measured}.

Pseudocode for the research adapter:

```text
save the complete old state and auxiliary post-processing data
propose a native implicit step no larger than the current maximum
record raw cell terms, native residual, profiles and acceptance fields
if every scientific gate passes: commit state and auxiliary data
otherwise: restore both, halve the proposal, retain the rejection
stop if the minimum step or attempt budget is exhausted
recover the step gradually, never beyond the declared maximum
```

[372,141 accepted proposals and 2,659 rejected proposals are retained in 23,100 raw chunks; rejected-step rollback and retry schedules pass reconstruction]{.claim}[C-308](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-308){.cid .st-measured}. The raw auditor checks the retry schedule and cross-step
profile continuity, including rejected old-state identity. Accepted density
representations receive only the documented floating-point conversion allowance;
rejected old-state drift remains a failure. Complete auxiliary-state rollback is
enforced by the frozen retry source and synthetic controls. Per-trial profile
records alone do not independently certify every auxiliary leaf.

The reusable opt-in module has an older global-only acceptance helper. The
successful ensemble instead uses the frozen research `runner.py` and
`advance.py`, which add the channelwise and native residual gates and stop on
an event. A caller of the reusable module does not automatically inherit this
full validation protocol.

| Continuous transition | [input and wrapper transitions span 10^−4^ of their stored ranges, the low heat-coefficient fade spans 0.01 m²/s, upper-cap fades use 1% of the cap, and the particle switch spans 10% of its existing threshold]{.claim}[C-310](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-310){.cid .st-measured} |
| Retry and reporting | [each macro step allows 64 proposals down to one 4096th of its maximum step, rejects by halving and recovers by at most doubling; common reporting times are 0.1, 0.4, 1, 3, 4.25 and 5 seconds]{.claim}[C-311](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-311){.cid .st-measured} |
| Scientific acceptance | [maximum accepted physical-channel L1 is 1.76 × 10^−9^ against a 10^−8^ gate, and native mean L1 is 1.01 × 10^−14^ against 10^−10^; no crash occurs]{.claim}[C-307](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-307){.cid .st-measured} |

The numerical solver stop is distinct from the scientific physical acceptance
threshold. Neither is relaxed after seeing an endpoint comparison. Transition
widths are declared model parameters; their fixed values in this experiment do
not establish width robustness.

## Full ensemble protocol and result {#full-ensemble-convergence}

[all 33 original cases reach five seconds at all three maximum-step settings: 99 of 99 valid trajectories and 264 of 264 passing endpoint comparisons]{.claim}[C-305](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-305){.cid .st-measured}. The declared maximum steps are halved successively while
holding the continuous closure, its transition widths, radial smoothing, original
case design and ensemble member assignment fixed. Every trajectory starts from
its own prescribed initial state. Saved complete state/post checkpoints restart
reporting stages without substituting profile-only states.

At the common final time, compute for each quantity $Q$

$$
\delta_Q(h,h/2)=\frac{|Q_h-Q_{h/2}|}{\max(|Q_{h/2}|,\operatorname{tiny}_{64})}.
$$

Both adjacent pairs must pass for fusion power, stored thermal energy, and axis
electron and ion temperature. This is sensitivity to an adaptive maximum step;
actual accepted internal steps can be smaller. It is not an estimate of fixed-step
order or an exact-solution bound. [the largest changes are 0.219% for coarse-to-middle and 0.0423% for middle-to-fine, both below the 1% acceptance limit]{.claim}[C-306](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-306){.cid .st-measured}.

missing cases, changed endpoints and incomplete comparisons.

## What the pass changes

The current baseline meets its full ensemble numerical gate. The earlier
checkpoint-only statement that no complete convergence study exists is now
superseded by this result. The checkpoint damping and learned-selector sections
below remain the history that led to the classical method; no learned solver
benefit is claimed.

The next uncertainty/sensitivity propagation must explicitly adopt this baseline
and retain its complete sampling design. The earlier uncertainty outputs were
not silently rerun. Matched smoothing-width studies, derivative behavior and any
direct particle-flux prototype are separate work. Physical-model acceptance and
M5 physicist sign-off remain pending. Reverse-mode differentiation through the
adaptive retry decisions is unsupported; this pass does not validate gradients.

## Earlier checkpoint experiments

The following sections describe the earlier fixed-context experiments, not the
current completed trajectory protocol.

## Checkpoint controller {#checkpoint-controller}

The independent same-state operator audit identifies a discrete stabilization
contribution from convection interpolation. This is distinct from the observed
surrogate/fallback alternation. Damping can change iteration behavior while
preserving the stabilized map's different nonlinear target.

Let A denote the current stabilized implicit matrix. Let R be storage minus the
physical transport/source equation, evaluated at the same state and complete
pre-step context. Scale R by the same transient coefficients and time step used
in its physical theta equation. A correction direction solves

```text
A(x) delta = -s_physical(x) R_physical(x).
x_trial = x + alpha delta.
```

For nonsingular A and nonzero transient scale, a zero direction requires a
physical root. This target-preservation identity is not a convergence theorem.
The original transport model, guard, boundary conditions and sources stay fixed.

The prototype compares original Picard, fixed damping, residual backtracking,
regularized Anderson and physical-defect backtracking. All trials start from the
same checkpoint guess. Complete old/new canonical state leaves preserve context;
profile-only records are never treated as restarts. No trial advances a canonical
trajectory. Separate thermal, density and flux residuals retain their units.

Each channel's reference scale is its initial cell-width integral of absolute
storage, combined transport RHS, and combined source/pinning RHS. Freeze that
scale during the solve. Candidate merit is the largest normalized channel L1
residual. Reject invalid or insufficiently decreasing candidates. Undefined
reference scales remain explicit failures. Algorithmic residual tolerances do
not replace the unchanged endpoint temporal criterion.

The learned component classifies a finite grid of damping factors. Inputs contain
separate physical/stabilized residual norms, recent branch change, distance to
the surrogate domain and time step. Complete classical search grids produce
labels; a failed grid has no class label. Whole-case holdouts govern direction
selection, feature normalization and fitting. An explicit training input box
routes unfamiliar inputs to classical backtracking. Residual checks decide every
accepted proposal and every convergence flag.

Focused controls cover cycling, biased stabilized roots, absent physical roots,
unit scaling, failed proposals and data separation ([focused numerical, data-separation and short TORAX checks pass; early-time full-step labels validate plumbing, not learned benefit or a numerical remedy]{.claim}[C-302](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-302){.cid .st-tested}). Short
real-code checks retain canonical trace and predictor/corrector parity. These
early-time examples have only full-step labels and establish no learned benefit.
At that checkpoint, the full late experiment remained prepared for review.
The later complete trajectory result is reported above; it uses the classical
strict solve and a changed continuous closure, without a learned damping policy.

Related work includes [neural fixed-point acceleration](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.10254)
and [solver-in-the-loop training](https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.00016). This prototype
uses classical rollout labels and held-out controller rollouts; it does not train
end to end through the discontinuous guard. The cited demonstrations do not
establish guarantees for this transport equation.

Narrative companion: entry 96, private draft.

## Retained compensation and damping results {#checkpoint-results}

The later fixed-context comparison retains original Picard, compensated updates
and half-damped compensated updates. The finer-stage execution failed one
historical storage comparison after saving all trial records. Small changes in
pre-subtraction operands are consistent with cancellation amplifying the observed
storage difference. The original failed gate is not waived or relabelled a pass.
Separate dense/FV reconstruction checks the retained physical targets, unrelaxed
linear solves, actual relaxation updates and guard selections.

The passing coarse-stage cycling example has a lower physical residual under
compensation and a further reduction with half damping ([at the matched passing coarse cycling checkpoint, the electron residual is 9.148% originally, 6.885% after compensation and 2.228% with half damping; nominal states can converge more slowly with damping]{.claim}[C-303](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-303){.cid .st-preliminary}).
At nominal checkpoints the corrected undamped map reduces that residual faster.
These are finite fixed-old-state comparisons, not new trajectories or endpoint
error estimates. Fine-stage comparisons remain qualified diagnostic evidence.

A separate small selector uses only the passing coarse stage and holds out each
whole case. Initial physical/stabilized channel residuals and the domain-boundary
margin are inputs; later residuals supply labels only. The output selects one
fixed damping factor for the entire retained update budget. It is not an adaptive
per-iteration controller. The held-out choices provide no reliable advantage over
the full-step compensated baseline, and most unfamiliar inputs use that baseline.

Do not construct per-iteration action labels by pairing equal iteration indices
from the two fixed-alpha paths: those paths have different states. Actual paired
action evaluations and branch histories are needed before learning an adaptive
policy. Compensated residual backtracking is the next classical comparison.
